clinician.final_diagnosis: Primary cutaneous anaplastic large cell lymphoma (C-ALCL)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 73-year-old man presented with a rapidly enlarging exophytic skin tumor in the right parotideomasseteric region after prior diagnosis and treatment for discoid lupus erythematosus. Initial biopsy histopathology indicated pilomatrix carcinoma. Subsequent immunohistochemical studies revealed large anaplastic cells positive for LCA, CD30, and negative for ALK, consistent with C-ALCL. CT imaging showed no lymphoma involvement in other organs, confirming the diagnosis of primary cutaneous ALCL without systemic disease.
